claims.text: Adding 1–3 at.% interstitial carbon to a single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy will induce controlled lattice distortion.
The carbon-induced distortion may be a slight tetragonal or fcc-to-fct-like distortion.
Lowering the symmetry of the fcc lattice increases magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
The high symmetry of a cubic lattice limits intrinsic magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Carbon atoms occupying interstitial sites produce localized lattice strain.
Strain-induced anisotropy enhancement strengthens domain-wall pinning.
Interstitial carbon will create effective domain-wall pinning sites in the proposed FeCoNi-based alloy.
The enhanced anisotropy will raise the energy barrier for domain-wall motion.
Carbon addition will increase the coercive field to well above 100 Oe.
High saturation magnetization will be largely retained after carbon addition.
The baseline single-phase fcc FeCoNi alloy has high saturation magnetization and a coercive field of approximately 100 Oe.
Controlled melt-spinning or rapid solidification followed by heat treatment can incorporate 1–3 at.% carbon into the fcc lattice.
The proposed carbon range and processing can preserve a predominantly single-phase fcc or slightly distorted structure without secondary carbide precipitation.
The carbon concentration that maximizes anisotropy without carbide precipitation depends on processing conditions.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires coercivity well above 100 Oe, but the falsification rule focuses on absence of a statistically significant increase and equates that with remaining near or below 100 Oe. A statistically significant but small increase only slightly above 100 Oe would fail the stated prediction without clearly triggering falsification.
